comparison: Both evaluate the finite element analysis methodology and functional interpretations (C44-C52). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to methodological concerns (scaling assumptions, muscle force estimates, material properties, lack of validation), while peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, praising the integration of methods and compelling eco-morphological results without raising these technical concerns.

Both address isotopic evidence for diet and habitat (C37-C43, with peer also including C72). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED but notes lack of statistical testing and detailed error analysis. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, praising the integration of isotopic data with other methods as providing compelling results without mentioning statistical limitations.

Both evaluate narial morphology and trunk evolution evidence (C53-C62 for OpenEval; C53-C66 for peer including PCA results). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes functional interpretations are inferences needing biomechanical validation, while peer reviewers praise the co-evolutionary findings as fundamental contributions addressing trunk-mandible relationships.

Both evaluate the connection between proboscidean evolution and climate change (C73-C77, with OpenEval also including C78-C79). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the synthesis extends beyond what can be definitively proven, while peer reviewers explicitly identify elucidating evolutionary responses to climate change as a fundamental contribution.

Both address fossil abundance and temporal patterns (C28-C36 for OpenEval; these plus biogeographic context C86-C89 for peer). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes lack of detailed statistical analysis and potential sampling biases, while peer reviewers praise the fundamental findings on diversification without raising these concerns.

Both evaluate background context and taxonomic framework (C6-C10 for OpenEval; C6-C13 for peer including phylogenetic analysis). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval describes these as well-established facts from literature, while peer reviewers praise the comprehensive inclusion of Asian bunodont proboscideans and supplementary materials.

Both evaluate main conclusions integrating all evidence (C1, C5, C80-C85 for OpenEval; C1-C5, C78-C85 for peer). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes evolutionary scenarios involve inference about functional transitions that cannot be directly observed, while peer reviewers describe these as fundamental findings that are very well supported.

Both address morphological evidence from fossils (C11-C23 for OpenEval; C14-C27 for peer including mandibular morphology and functional interpretations). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval provides detailed assessment of phylogenetic support and specimen documentation, while peer reviewers praise the well-supported and well-illustrated approach.

Both evaluate synthesis of feeding ecology evidence (C2-C4, C67-C69, C71-C72 for OpenEval; C67-C71 for peer). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the functional shift from mandible to trunk is an inference that cannot be directly tested, while peer reviewers accept these synthetic interpretations as successfully addressing core questions about trunk-mandible relationships and diet patterns.

OpenEval evaluates mandibular morphology and functional interpretations (C24-C27) as UNCERTAIN due to speculative nature of keratinous cutting plate inference lacking direct evidence. Peer result R3 includes these claims (C24-C27) within broader morphological descriptions rated as SUPPORTED, with no specific concerns raised about these functional interpretations.

Both address PCA results linking narial evolution to horizontal cutting (C63-C66). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes lack of correlation coefficients or statistical tests for relationship strength, while peer reviewers accept these as part of compelling co-evolutionary findings without raising statistical concerns.

Both address biogeographic context (C70, C86-C89). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes Tibetan Plateau uplift connection is reasonable inference with complex unresolved mechanisms, while peer reviewers integrate this biogeographic context with temporal patterns as fundamental findings on diversification and climate responses.

OpenEval R1 addresses morphological evidence and phylogenetic analysis (C11-C23), while peer R2 addresses background context and taxonomic framework (C6-C13). Overlap on C11-C13 (phylogenetic analysis). Both rate as SUPPORTED, with OpenEval emphasizing phylogenetic support values and peer reviewers praising comprehensive taxonomic coverage.

OpenEval R8 evaluates feeding ecology synthesis (C2-C4, C67-C69, C71-C72), while peer R1 evaluates main conclusions (C1-C5, C78-C85). Overlap on C2-C4. Both rate as SUPPORTED, with OpenEval noting some interpretations remain speculative while peer reviewers describe as fundamental findings on evolutionary transitions.

OpenEval R9 addresses climate-evolution connections (C73-C79), while peer R1 addresses main conclusions (C1-C5, C78-C85). Overlap on C78-C79. Both rate as SUPPORTED, with OpenEval noting synthesis extends beyond definitive proof while peer reviewers accept as fundamental findings on evolutionary responses to climate.

OpenEval R12 addresses biogeographic context (C70, C86-C89), while peer R8 addresses feeding ecology synthesis (C67-C71). Overlap on C70. Both rate as SUPPORTED, with minimal overlap indicating these results address largely different aspects of the evidence.
